a1-adj-muede: It is midnight, you have worked all day and your eyes keep closing. You can hardly wait to get into bed.
A baby yawns and rubs her eyes after a long afternoon of playing. How does she feel?
At the end of a long journey your friend says that he has no energy left and needs rest. Which adjective means 'tired'?
a1-v-fliegen: You sit on a plane and look down at the clouds as it moves through the air at 10,000 metres.
A bird opens its wings and rises into the sky above the trees.
You go from Berlin to Rome in two hours, not by train or by car. Which verb means 'to fly'?
a1-n-tag: A clock goes round twice, which makes twenty-four hours. What is this period of time called?
Between sunrise and sunset it is light outside. What do you call this time, the opposite of night?
Monday is the first one of the week. Which noun means 'day'?
a1-n-baeckerei: Early in the morning you walk to a small shop and buy fresh bread rolls and a loaf for breakfast.
A shop smells of warm bread and cakes. A woman behind the counter puts rolls into a paper bag.
You need bread for dinner and your friend says: 'Go to the shop on the corner where they bake it.' Which noun means 'bakery'?
a1-adv-sehr: The soup is extremely hot, so you wait before you eat it. Which small word makes the adjective stronger?
A friend gives you a present and you say: 'Thank you so much, I like it a lot.'
The film was not just good, it was to a high degree good. Which adverb means 'very'?
a1-n-e-mail: You do not write a letter on paper. You type a message on your computer and send it to your boss's address with an @ sign.
The teacher asks for your electronic address so she can send you the homework.
On the form there is a line for your address with an @ in it. Which noun means 'email'?
a1-v-tanzen: At the party the music starts and you move your body to the rhythm with your friends on the floor.
At a wedding the bride and groom open the floor and move together to a slow song.
At a club your friend says: 'Let's go and move to the music!' Which verb means 'to dance'?
a1-n-firma: Your father works for a business with a hundred employees that makes cars.
A sign on the building shows the name of the organisation that sells computers and has an office on the third floor.
At an interview the boss asks: 'Why do you want to work for our organisation?' Which noun means 'company'?
a1-pr-dir: You hand a friend a present and say: 'This is for ...' Which informal word means 'to you'?
You ask a friend: 'Can I give ... a lift to the station?' Which word means 'you' (informal, after 'to')?
A child's mother says: 'Do you feel better? How is it going for ... ?' Which informal pronoun means 'you'?
a1-n-stock: In an apartment building you live on the third level above the ground floor. Which noun do you use for a level of a building?
An old man walks slowly in the park and leans on a long piece of wood in his hand.
In the lift there are buttons for each level of the building. Which noun can mean 'floor' (of a building) or 'stick'?
a1-adj-klar: The water in the lake is so clean that you can see the bottom. How is the water?
The teacher explains the task and everyone says that they understand it very well. Nothing is confusing.
After a rainy day the sky has no clouds at all. Which adjective means 'clear'?
a1-v-aufhoeren: The rain has been falling all day. At six o'clock it finally does not fall any more.
The teacher says: 'Please do not talk any more, the lesson has begun.' What should the students do?
Your doctor says you should not smoke any more. You give it up. Which verb means 'to stop, to cease'?
a1-n-hausmann: A man stays at home while his wife goes to work. He cooks, cleans and takes the children to school.
On a form for a man there is the job: he takes care of the home and the children.
Your neighbour says: 'My husband does not have a job outside, he runs our home.' Which noun means 'house husband'?
a1-n-apartment: You rent a small home in a big building in the city, with one room, a kitchen and a bathroom.
A friend from America says that he lives in a small home on the sixth floor of a tower.
A website shows modern homes for rent in the city centre. Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'apartment'?
a1-n-haar: At the hairdresser's you ask her to cut your locks, which are growing on your head.
In the shower you wash the strands that grow on your head with shampoo.
A friend says: 'You have a thin line growing on your jacket from your cat.' Which noun means 'hair' (a single one)?
a1-v-anrufen: You pick up your phone, type your friend's number and wait until she answers.
The boss says to the secretary: 'Please ring the customer and tell him that the delivery is late.'
You want to reserve a table. You take your phone and dial the number of the restaurant. Which verb means 'to call, to phone'?
a1-adv-wohin: A friend says: 'I am going away on holiday.' You ask about the destination of the trip.
You see your colleague with a suitcase and ask him about the place he is going to.
At the station a tourist asks you about the direction of your journey. Which question word means 'where to'?
a1-n-deutsche: A man from Hamburg has a passport from Germany. How do you call him?
At the border the officer asks a man for his passport. The man says that he is from Munich. Which noun describes his nationality?
At a conference people from many countries meet. A man from Berlin introduces himself. Which noun means 'German' (male person)?
a1-n-freundin: A girl and you spend a lot of time together, you share secrets and laugh together. She is not your sister.
A man says: 'Tonight I will take the woman I am in love with to dinner.'
A woman says about the person she has known since school: 'We tell each other everything.' Which noun means 'friend' or 'girlfriend' (female)?
a1-adj-neu: You have bought a phone today, so it is not old and has never been used before.
You start your first day in a different job and meet colleagues you have not met yet.
The opposite of old: your friend wears a coat that she bought yesterday. Which adjective means 'new'?
a1-n-tochter: A man points to the little girl next to him and says that she is the female child of him and his wife.
At the parents' evening the teacher talks to a mother about her female child, who is eight years old.
You have one son and one girl. Which noun means 'daughter'?
a1-v-uebernachten: You travel far and sleep in a hostel for one night before you continue the next morning.
Your friend lives in another city. You stay at her flat for the night, because the last train has gone.
A hotel sign says: 'Overnight stays from 50 euros.' Which verb means 'to spend the night'?
a1-n-grossvater: An old man with white hair plays chess with a child. He is the father of the child's mother.
A boy says: 'My dad's dad lives in a small village and has a big garden.'
At the family dinner the oldest man at the table is the father of your father. Which noun means 'grandfather'?
a1-n-termin: You call the dentist's office and get a fixed time, Tuesday at 3 p.m., for your check-up.
Your boss asks you to write a note in your calendar for the meeting with the customer on Friday.
The project must be handed in by the end of the month. Which noun can mean 'appointment' or 'deadline'?
a1-n-hilfe: You fall off your bike and shout so that someone will come and assist you.
The old woman cannot carry her bags and says: 'Thank you for your hand.'
You carry a heavy sofa and ask your neighbour for support. Which noun means 'help'?
a1-v-haben: You have two brothers and one sister. How would you say that these people are part of your family?
At the till the clerk asks if you possess a loyalty card. You say that you do.
A friend says: 'I am hungry because I do not possess any food at home.' Which verb means 'to have'?
a1-adj-normal: The doctor looks at your test results and says that nothing is unusual.
Your friend asks if the strange noise from the car is a problem. The mechanic says that this is the usual sound.
The teacher says: 'Today is an ordinary day, there is no test.' Which adjective means 'normal'?
a1-n-geschaeft: On the main street you walk past a place where you can buy clothes, shoes and gifts.
Your uncle runs a place that sells furniture. He opens it every morning at nine.
A company signs an important agreement with another company about buying and selling. Which noun can mean 'shop' or 'business deal'?
a1-adv-da: You point at a chair in the corner and say: 'The keys are on the chair, they are ...' Which adverb means 'there'?
Your friend asks: 'Are you at home?' You answer: 'Yes, I am present.' Which short word means 'here, there'?
A child looks into a box and says: 'Look, it is ...!' Which adverb means 'there'?
a1-pr-ihnen: You speak about your neighbours: 'I gave the book to ...' Which word means 'to them'?
Your friends are lost and call you. You say: 'I will show the way to ...' Which pronoun means 'to them'?
You tell a story about the children: 'My mother gave sweets to ...' Which word means 'them'?
a1-n-strassenbahn: In many cities a long vehicle with wires above runs on rails in the middle of the street and stops at stops.
You take an electric vehicle in the street that goes on tracks, not underground, and costs less than a taxi.
In Berlin, Vienna and Prague you can see yellow or red vehicles on rails in the road. Which noun means 'tram'?
a1-v-rauchen: A man stands outside the office and lights a cigarette. Smoke comes out of his mouth.
The sign in the restaurant says that you are not allowed to do this inside, where the air must stay clean.
The doctor says that you should not do what puts tobacco smoke in your lungs. Which verb means 'to smoke'?
a1-n-vermieter: You rent a flat. Each month you send the money to the man who owns the building.
The heating is broken. You call the man who owns the house and ask him to send a plumber.
A tenant says: 'The man who let me this flat is very friendly.' Which noun means 'landlord'?
a1-n-norden: On a compass the needle points to the top of the map. Which direction is this?
You live in Munich and your friend lives in Hamburg, a long way up the map. In which direction is Hamburg?
A weather forecaster says: 'It will be cold in the upper part of the country.' Which noun means 'north'?
a1-n-europaeer: A man from Italy and a man from Poland meet. They both come from the same continent.
At the airport there are two lines: one for people with passports from the EU countries, and one for others.
A tourist from Asia says: 'In Paris, Rome and Berlin I met many people from this continent.' Which noun means 'European' (male)?
a1-v-sprechen: You ring your friend and for an hour you use your voice to say things on the phone.
The teacher asks: 'Do you want to use German in the conversation, or English?'
At the meeting the manager says words into the microphone for ten minutes. Which verb means 'to speak'?
a1-adj-verboten: The sign on the wall shows a cigarette with a red line. It is against the rules to do it here.
At the pool a sign says that you may not jump in from the side. Which adjective describes this action?
The police officer says that parking here is against the law. Which adjective means 'forbidden'?
a1-n-student: A young man goes to lectures at the university and writes exams. He is learning to become an engineer.
On the bus a young man shows a card and gets a discount because he studies at the university.
A friend says about his brother: 'He is at university, he studies medicine.' Which noun means 'student' (male)?
a1-n-unterschrift: At the bottom of the contract there is a line where you must write your name by hand.
The postman gives you a parcel and asks you to put your name on his phone screen.
On the form the clerk says: 'Please write your name here, with your pen, at the end.' Which noun means 'signature'?
a1-adv-links: You stand at the crossing. To reach the bakery you must turn to the side of your body where your heart is.
A driver says: 'Take the next turn on the side that is not the right one.'
The taxi driver asks: 'Right or ... ?' Which adverb means 'left'?
a1-n-kasse: At the supermarket you put your shopping on a belt and then pay the person who scans it.
At the cinema you queue in front of the window where you buy a ticket.
At the end of your shopping trip you queue at the place where everyone pays. Which noun means 'checkout, till'?
a1-v-einsteigen: The bus stops at the stop and you step through the door to take your seat.
The taxi arrives. You open the door and sit inside.
The announcement says: 'The train to Hamburg is ready, please go aboard.' Which verb means 'to board, to get on'?
a1-n-computer: You sit at your desk and type a report on a machine with a screen and a keyboard.
At school the children learn how to write a program on a machine in the classroom.
A friend says: 'My laptop is broken, and I need a new one.' Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'computer'?
a1-n-aerztin: You have a headache and a fever. You make an appointment with a woman in a white coat who examines you.
A friend says: 'My aunt works at the hospital and treats sick people.' Which word is used for a female medical person like her?
Your child is sick and you call a woman who can treat her. Which noun means 'doctor' (female)?
a1-adj-boese: A child breaks a plate and her father's face turns red. He shouts. How does he feel?
In the fairy tale the witch wants to harm the princess. What kind of person is the witch?
Your neighbour is upset because someone parked in front of her garage. Which adjective can mean 'angry' or 'evil'?
a1-v-sagen: You open your mouth and tell your friend the news that you got a new job.
A child asks: 'What did the teacher tell you yesterday?' You repeat the words.
The boss wants to know the reason. You give him your answer in words. Which verb means 'to say'?
a1-n-mittag: The sun is at its highest point and the clock shows twelve. What time of day is it?
The school canteen opens at twelve and the children go to eat their main meal.
A shop sign says: 'Closed from 12 to 2.' Which noun means 'noon, midday'?
a1-n-post: Every morning a man in a yellow uniform brings letters and parcels to your door.
You must send a parcel to your brother in another country, so you go to a building with counters and stamps.
You put a stamp on a card and drop it into the yellow box. Which noun means 'mail' or 'post office'?
a1-pr-nichts: You look in the fridge and there is not a single thing to eat. Which word describes what you find?
The teacher asks: 'What did you learn today?' You are embarrassed and say that you learned zero things. Which pronoun is that?
A friend asks what is in the box. You open it and it is empty. Which word means 'nothing'?
a1-n-eintrittskarte: At the entrance of the museum you pay and the clerk gives you a small piece of paper that lets you go in.
You are going to a concert. At the box office you buy a paper that you must show at the door.
You want to go to the zoo. Which noun means the 'ticket' for entering a place, not for a train?
a1-v-verkaufen: You put your old bike on the internet. A man pays you 100 euros and rides away on it.
A baker stands behind the counter and gives bread to customers in return for money.
You do not need your old phone any more and give it to someone who pays you for it. Which verb means 'to sell'?
a1-n-wort: The teacher writes 'house' on the board and asks you to say it in another language. What did she write?
A sentence is made up of many small units. You do not know the meaning of one of them, so you look it up in the dictionary.
You learn new vocabulary every day. Which noun means 'word'?
a1-adv-geradeaus: A man asks you for the way to the station. You say: 'Go along this street and don't turn left or right.'
The satnav says to keep going in the same direction for two kilometres.
At the traffic light a tourist asks: 'Do I turn here?' You say: 'No, keep going forward.' Which adverb means 'straight ahead'?
a1-n-polizei: A thief takes your bag. You dial 110 and officers in uniform arrive at the scene.
After a car accident, a man in a blue uniform writes down what happened.
A child is lost in the town. The mother asks officers in a car with blue lights for help. Which noun means 'police'?
a1-adj-gleich: You and your friend buy the same shirt in the same colour and size. They look just alike.
In class all students get the same task, and nobody gets a different one.
Two plus two and one plus three give the same result. Which adjective means 'same, equal'?
a1-n-reisefuehrer: Before your trip to Italy you buy a book with maps, tips and information about hotels and sights.
A tourist walks around Rome with a thick book in his hand and reads about the history of each building.
At the bookshop you ask for a book that gives advice for visitors to Spain. Which noun means 'guidebook'?
a1-v-baden: It is Saturday evening. You fill the tub with hot water and lie in it to relax.
On a hot day at the beach you go into the sea to cool down.
You wash your little baby in a small plastic tub with warm water. Which verb means 'to bathe'?
a1-n-milch: For breakfast you pour a white liquid from a bottle into your cereal. It comes from cows.
A baby is hungry and her mother gives her a bottle of a white drink.
At the supermarket you buy a carton from the fridge section. It is white and you pour it into your tea. Which noun means 'milk'?
